knowledge_point.title: Using Alternative Forms of Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Expressions

question.:question/problem: Express $2\cos^2\left(\frac{13\pi}{7}\right)-1$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the alternative cosine double-angle formula:

$$
2\cos^2 x-1=\cos(2x)
$$

Substitute $x=\frac{13\pi}{7}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
2\cos^2\left(\frac{13\pi}{7}\right)-1&=\cos\left(2\cdot \frac{13\pi}{7}\right)\\&=\cos\left(\frac{26\pi}{7}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Express $\frac{3}{2}-3\sin^2\left(\frac{17\pi}{11}\right)$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Collect the common factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{3}{2}-3\sin^2\left(\frac{17\pi}{11}\right)\\&=\frac{3}{2}\left(1-2\sin^2\left(\frac{17\pi}{11}\right)\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

Use the alternative cosine double-angle formula:

$$
1-2\sin^2 x=\cos(2x)
$$

Substitute $x=\frac{17\pi}{11}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
1-2\sin^2\left(\frac{17\pi}{11}\right)&=\cos\left(2\cdot \frac{17\pi}{11}\right)\\&=\cos\left(\frac{34\pi}{11}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

Keep the outside factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{3}{2}\left(1-2\sin^2\left(\frac{17\pi}{11}\right)\right)&=\frac{3}{2}\cos\left(\frac{34\pi}{11}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Using Alternative Forms of Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Expressions

question.:question/problem: Express $-\frac{3}{4}+\frac{3}{2}\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi}{5}\right)$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Collect the common factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&-\frac{3}{4}+\frac{3}{2}\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi}{5}\right)\\&=\frac{3}{4}\left(2\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi}{5}\right)-1\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

Use the alternative cosine double-angle formula:

$$
2\cos^2 x-1=\cos(2x)
$$

Substitute $x=\frac{\pi}{5}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
2\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi}{5}\right)-1&=\cos\left(2\cdot \frac{\pi}{5}\right)\\&=\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{5}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

Keep the outside factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{3}{4}\left(2\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi}{5}\right)-1\right)&=\frac{3}{4}\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{5}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$
